_comment: The popularity bar, pinned end to end. The declaration is fetchable AND the bytes match exactly - the only thing wrong is that the package is not widely used (12 downloads a month, well under the bar). So verifyUrl returns 'not-popular', the file joins the untrusted family, and because it is minified nothing can review it: untrusted-minified-library rejects. That is the policy - only popular libraries are trusted, everything else is the developer's own work - and this is the only fixture that reaches 'not-popular'; an unfetchable declaration lands on the same report for a different reason. The triple this completes: verified-vendor-source (matches, popular -> exempt), vendor-modified (fetchable, popular, bytes differ -> reject), this (matches, popular enough? no -> reject).
